title: Real Play as an Alternative to Screens: Exploring the World with the Five Senses
summary: A child under three learns through sensory exploration: touch, taste, smell, hearing, and sight. Screens confine them to just two senses (sight/hearing) and neglect the rest. Data on children’s device usage confirms: the more screen time, the less free play, movement, and social interaction. Unstructured play (free play) develops executive functions, problem-solving, and creativity—skills no app can teach. Your role: provide a safe, stimulating environment rich with materials (boxes, fabrics, nature, water), and gradually step back to let your child direct their own play.
try_this: This week: Prepare a weekly 'exploration basket'—change its contents every 3 days (first: plastic kitchen tools, second: fabrics of different textures, third: natural elements like rocks, leaves, and shells). Observe: How many minutes does he play independently? What attracts him most?
reflection_prompts: What was the most engaging toy/activity for your child this week, and why?
Do you feel anxious when leaving your child to play alone? How do you overcome this feeling?
